sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2013. The Gelao languages: Preliminary classification and state of the art. Presentation, ICSTLL 46. Zenodo, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.2533289
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.note: Classification slides only; no phonology. Names the sources for Green Gelao (Hakei): Pomao = Zhou Guoyan (1999), Sanchong = Shen Yumay (2003) and Guangxi Minority Languages (2008); Hakei (Guizhou) c. 2,000 speakers in Guanling, Zhenning, Qinglong; Hakei (Sanchong) 300. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2011. Change Request 2011-054 (split of Gelao [gio]; giq = Green Gelao/Hagei). SIL International
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.note: Identity only: 'Hagei dialect in Gelao is the same language as Green Gelao [giq]', spoken in Guizhou and in Sanchong village, Longlin County, Guangxi (citing He 1983). No phonology.

sources.citation: Ostapirat, Weera. 2000. Proto-Kra. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 23(1): 1-251 (special issue). DOI 10.15144/LTBA-23.1.1
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.note: Comparative reconstruction (Proto-Kra tones, initials, finals). Section 2.6 'Gelao varieties' (p. 29) treats Hagei: Yangliu (Renhuai) = Green Gelao/Hagei, Sanchong (Longlin, Guangxi) with a 'concise corpus' from Edmondson & Thurgood (1992), Qinglong per He (1983); Sanchong and Qinglong merge proto tone classes B and C. Nothing about stress or accent in the 44 scanned pages; the rest of the 251-page scan was not scanned.

sources.citation: Coyaud, Maurice. 1987. Les langues dans le monde chinois. Paris: P.A.F. Section 3.7 'Gelao', pp. 161-162 (Rosetta Project scan)
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.note: Not Hagei: a two-page sketch of Anshun (Qau) Gelao after He Jiashan 1981. Lists six tones ('trois tons plats: 55, 44, 33 et trois tons obliques: 24, 13, 31'), consonants, finals, clusters. No mention of stress/accent.
